title: Siri AI's Biggest Upgrade Yet + John Ternus's First Apple Earnings Call
summary:
Apple is finally bringing some of Siri's most ambitious AI capabilities to the iPhone. In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and Vlad Savov break down the major changes coming with iOS 27.3, including Siri's new ability to control apps, carry out complex tasks and coordinate actions across multiple applications. They discuss how these improvements compare with AI agents from OpenAI and Meta, and why Apple still has a long way to go. Plus, Mark and Vlad analyze John Ternus's first earnings call as Apple's CEO, the company's strong iPhone sales, concerns about slowing growth and profit margins, and why more price increases could be coming. They also examine Apple's AI rollout in China and the privacy implications of new always-listening Apple Watch features.

Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord
Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Google AI in School Triggered Teen’s Mental Health Crisis, Lawsuit Says
summary: Parents in North Carolina sued Google after their 13-year-old daughter spent months discussing suicidal thoughts with the company’s artificial intelligence tools on her school-issued Chromebook, underscoring the potential risks of the technology as parents and educators debate AI’s place in schools.

title: Colony: AI Investment Will Continue Despite Tech Selloff
summary: George Colony, Forrester Research Founder, Chairman & CEO says the AI boom may be entering a new phase. Custom chips could challenge Nvidia's dominance, while value shifts toward software. But the transition won't be smooth: companies must adapt to AI computing, or risk being left behind. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Bets Meet Higher Capital Costs
summary: As the cost of capital rises,  David N. Miller says private markets still see opportunity, from flexible financing for hard-to-refinance assets to infrastructure beyond the AI boom. He discusses AI's long-term potential, concentration risks, and why selectivity matters for investors. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rio Tinto Backs Major Copper Project
summary: Rio Tinto is committing $144 million to advance the Resolution Copper project in Arizona, funding additional drilling, engineering and infrastructure work. The company says long-term copper demand is being driven not just by AI and data centers, but also electrification and everyday appliances, as the project moves toward key permits and a future investment decision.Vicky Peacey, president of Resolution Copper joins Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about the deal and what's ahead. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Musk’s Starlink Can Challenge AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile
summary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX has already transformed the internet-from-space business. Now, he’s taking on another entrenched industry with plans for a terrestrial wireless network to rival Verizon Communications Inc., T-Mobile US Inc. and AT&T Inc.

title: Oracle Data Center Developer Waives Key Air Permit Deadline
summary: The developer of power infrastructure for Oracle Corp.’s New Mexico data center agreed to delay a deadline for action on a key air permit, giving state environmental regulators more time to review it rather than deny the application.

title: State-Driven Data Center Backlash Reshaping the AI Trade
summary:
The Democratic sweep of Congress and a handful of governor races sent stock prices spiraling for so-called neoclouds. 
With contests swinging toward candidates promising tougher restrictions on building data centers and other infrastructure, investors and management teams are re-assessing the risk of increased cost and delayed timelines.
Brad Warden, Senior Portfolio Manager of Science and Tech Funds at Nomura, discusses AI cycle rotations and where the AI buildout could diverge post-Midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Zillow Moves on Weak Results; Dutch Bros Reduces Guidance | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Zillow (Z) is moving after it posted weaker-than-expected results and signaled that adjusted earnings in the next quarter could be the weakest in three years.
- Expedia (EXPE) shares are dropping even after the online travel agency raised its outlook for the full year. Still, the midpoint of its fourth-quarter gross bookings forecast trailed the average analyst estimate.
- Dutch Bros (BROS) shares sinking after the coffee chain cut its adjusted Ebitda forecast for the full year. The reduced guidance missed the average analyst estimate. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Selloff Is a 'Modest Wave' in a Multiyear Cycle, Bernstein's Chaloff Says
summary: Bernstein Private Wealth Management CIO Alex Chaloff says the selloff in AI stocks is creating buying opportunities in the market. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Microsoft Sours on Neoclouds IREN, Nebius, Nscale on Delays, Costs
summary: Microsoft Corp. helped create the “neocloud” boom, signing tens of billions of dollars in contracts with upstart data center operators in an effort to sate the crushing appetite for its cloud and AI services.

title: Sony Debuts Retro $60 Wired Headphones in Tribute to 1979 Walkman
summary: Sony Group Corp. introduced an inexpensive pair of wired headphones, joining a growing trend in what it called “a nod to both the ’80s Walkman era and today’s retro tech revival.”

title: Shield AI To Hit $28.8 Billion Value With $5.3 Billion Radar Acquisition
summary: Defense tech startup set to acquire Echodyne Corp., which sells radar sensors to government and commercial customers.

title: Chipmakers Selloff Leads Nasdaq 100 Down 5%
summary: Sarah Hunt, Alpine Saxon Woods chief market strategist, reacts to the chipmaker selloff which pulled down the Nasdaq 100 by 5% in early trading on Thursday. Some investors are worried a Democratic sweep of Congress could mean tighter regulation. She speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ex-Moore Money Manager to Return Cash From His Hedge Fund
summary: Paul Yablon, a former Moore Capital Management portfolio manager, is returning all external cash from his digital-focused hedge fund Room40 Capital.

title: Zipline Hits $20 Billion Valuation as Walmart Deal Expands
summary: Drone delivery startup Zipline closed a $1 billion funding round, valuing the company at $20 billion, as it expands its commercial partnership with Walmart in the US. Zipline CEO Keller Rinaudo speaks with Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow about what it took to grow the company to this point, how demand has shocked both Zipline and Walmart, and what comes next for the startup. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Microsoft Declined to Expand Texas Data Center Offer With Nscale Before IPO
summary: Microsoft Corp., one of Nscale’s primary customers, opted not to extend a contract at a Texas data center with the startup ahead of its planned public offering, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Amazon Adds Uber Food Delivery Perks for Prime Subscribers
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is adding Uber Technologies Inc. restaurant delivery perks on its shopping site for Prime members, forging a deeper partnership just a week after rival service DoorDash Inc. agreed to acquire Instacart.

title: Chips Selloff Worsens as Fears About AI Trade Grip Stock Market
summary: Shares of semiconductor stocks plunged on Thursday, extending a recent selloff as investors turn skeptical on the artificial intelligence trade after the Democrats dominated the midterm elections.

title: MercadoLibre Shares Tumble as Investments Weigh on Profit
summary: MercadoLibre Inc. shares plunge after the company posted third quarter earnings that missed profit estimates as investors weigh whether the company’s heavy investments translate into stronger profitability over the long run.
